# @k8ordo/ui

> React components from k8ordo, with semantic design tokens, dark mode,
> built-in Japanese/English wording, AI chat components, and official generative UI
> adapters (json-render & OpenUI) that let an LLM generate, validate, and render
> on-brand UIs from these components.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses only
> what has reached Baseline, and ships no polyfills or legacy fallbacks — so
> nothing here branches for a browser or a framework it does not support.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.
Start with the Design Guide, then follow the reference most relevant to the task.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/GUIDE.md): setup, i18n (default Japanese, switching to English), design direction, aesthetic guidelines, component usage principles, anti-patterns, implementation principles, testing in jsdom (components mount with no setup; the copy-paste `setupFiles` stubs for `ResizeObserver` / `IntersectionObserver` / `matchMedia` / `showModal` / the Popover API when a test needs to assert on open state).

## References

- [Components](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/components.md): full component list, import paths, props, and i18n — every component, compound ones included (`Dialog.Root`, `Tabs.Root`, …), renders from a Server Component — component wording comes from a dictionary that defaults to Japanese; `@k8ordo/ui/i18n` exports `ja` / `en` / the `Messages` type for `<UIProvider messages={...}>` (per-component wording props win over the dictionary).
- [AI chat](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/ai-chat.md): AI chat components from `@k8ordo/ui/ai` (Conversation / Message / PromptInput / Reasoning / Suggestion / ToolInvocation), streaming Markdown `Response` from `@k8ordo/ui/ai/response` (optional peer `streamdown`), and `mapMessageParts` from `@k8ordo/ui/ai-sdk` to render AI SDK `UIMessage.parts` (optional peer `ai`).
- [Generative UI](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/generative-ui.md): use json-render / OpenUI to make an LLM generate UIs — `catalog.prompt()` (server-safe), `<JsonRenderUI spec={spec} />` (client), `validateGeneratedSpec()` (validate/repair LLM output), `satisfies UISpec` (typed specs), and `@k8ordo/ui/openui/prompt`.
- [Typography](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/typography.md): type scale and usage.
- [Color](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/color.md): semantic token system and dark mode.
- [Spacing & layout](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/spatial-design.md): spacing scale and layout patterns.
- [Interaction](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/interaction-design.md): motion and interaction guidelines.
- [Hooks](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/hooks.md): custom hooks for UI mechanics (disclosure, timing, DOM observation). State that lives in a place (URL, history, localStorage, memory) belongs to `@k8ordo/state`, not to a hook here.
- [Helpers & types](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/helpers.md): the five helper functions (`chain` / `cn` / `createSafeContext` / `mergeProps` / `mergeRefs`) and the public types (`Status` / `Direction` / `Placement` / `ModalSide` / `DrawerSide` / `Option`).

# @k8ordo/form

> Derive HTML constraint attributes, error messages, and server-side validation
> from one zod schema. The DOM holds the values; React state holds only what the
> DOM cannot express. Forms work with JavaScript disabled or not yet loaded.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses only
> what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or legacy
> fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/form/docs/GUIDE.md): the server/client split, writing a form end to end,
  what the package guarantees, what it does not do yet, and how it pairs with
  `@k8ordo/ui` without depending on it.

## Not supported

`z.array(z.file())` derives repeated single-file rows, not one `multiple`
input. Constraints behind a `.transform()` (or a `.pipe()` whose output JSON
Schema cannot describe) are not derived: the field becomes a bare text input
and is listed in `dropped`. A `<select>` with a placeholder option behind
`.optional()` is still marked required. There is no input masking. A schema no
control could satisfy is refused at derive time rather than left to fail on
every submission: `z.number()` and `z.literal(1)` (use `z.coerce.number()`),
`z.date()`, `z.bigint()`.

## Entry points

- `@k8ordo/form` — client. `useForm(fields, state)` takes the whole
  `formFields` result and returns props for the `<form>` element, a
  `field(path)` accessor giving input attributes, the current error, and
  `invalid` / `required`, an `array(path)` accessor for repeated rows, and
  `isDirty`. Also `useAsyncCheck` for server-answered per-field checks and
  `HiddenValue` for components that render no input of their own. The types
  of the `formFields` result (`FormFields`, `DerivedField`, `DerivedArray`,
  `DroppedCheck`) are exported here as well, since the result crosses to the
  client as a prop.
- `@k8ordo/form/server` — server. `formFields(schema)` derives serializable
  fields plus a `dropped` list of checks HTML cannot express (outside
  production the list is also logged once per schema with `console.warn`),
  and throws on a schema no form can represent (including a leaf that could
  never accept a submitted string, such as `z.number()`);
  `parseForm(schema, formData)` validates a
  submission and returns typed data or per-field errors with the submitted
  values. An untouched control reaches the schema as what it actually submits:
  `''` for text, `false` for a checkbox, and nothing at all for a number or a
  file, so `z.coerce.number()` cannot read a blank field as 0.
  `defineForm(schema, rules)` attaches cross-field rules (`sameAs`,
  `minChecked`, `requiredWhen`) typed against the schema's paths.

---

# @k8ordo/state

> Declare state by where it lives: `definePageState` (typed URL search params
> plus hidden history-entry state — the two faces of one entry, updated
> atomically over the Navigation API), `defineLocalState` (localStorage,
> cross-tab), `defineMemoryState` (a typed shared box, resets on reload).
> One zod schema per place derives the server read, canonical links, salvage
> of stale data, and a client subscription with exact per-key change
> detection. Works through links and GET forms before JavaScript loads;
> imperative url updates ride a Navigation-API-intercepting router.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/state/docs/GUIDE.md): the four places and when each fits, the shared
  definition module, reading on the server, updating on the client, batching
  and update handles, subscription granularity, router requirements, typed
  routes via `Register`, reading local state before hydration, and pairing
  with `@k8ordo/form` for GET forms.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/state` — `definePageState(key, { url?, entry? })` returns a pure
  definition usable from server and client: `parseUrl(searchParams)` reads
  the url slot typed with defaults applied and per-field salvage (wherever the
  router hands a page its search — under `@k8ordo/static` / `@k8ordo/server` a
  page receives `params` and `pathname` only, and the url slot is read in the
  browser);
  `href(base, values?)` builds a canonical link keeping the path literal in
  the type; `search(values?)` returns the query string alone.
  `defineLocalState(key, schema)` and `defineMemoryState(key, initial)`
  declare app-scope state; a local definition also exposes `storageKey` (the
  localStorage key, `k8ordo-state:<key>`) and `inlineRead()`, a JavaScript
  expression for an inline `<script>` that evaluates to the stored object or
  `null` before hydration — unvalidated, so read only what you need with a
  fallback. `useAppState(definition, keys?, { initialUrl? })`
  (client) works on any kind and returns `[state, update]` — state is the
  flat merge of a page definition's slots; `update(patch)` applies
  synchronously, batches per handler into one write (url+entry atomically via
  `navigation.navigate()`, entry-only via `updateCurrentEntry()`, local via
  one `setItem`), and returns `{ committed, finished }` promise handles
  (settled for non-navigating kinds; `{ history: 'push' }` exists only on
  page state). `resetStateRegistry()` clears stores between tests. Augment
  `interface Register { routes: typeof routes }` — the same line as for
  `@k8ordo/router` — to constrain `href` paths to the route table's linkable
  paths; a router without a table registers its own path union as
  `interface Register { path }` instead.

---

# @k8ordo/router

> The URL's pathname axis, owned. One `defineRoutes` table is the application's
> pathname schema: types, matching, links and navigation all come from it, over
> the Navigation API and URLPattern. Search params and history-entry state are
> not its business — those belong to `@k8ordo/state`.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/router/docs/GUIDE.md): the table's grammar (leaves, branches, params,
  wildcards, route groups, declaration order), mounting `<Router>` and
  `<Outlet>`, links without a `<Link>` component, `useMatch` for active
  sections, `Register` for checked patterns, what navigation guarantees
  (`finished` after commit, scroll to top or fragment on a new page), and
  how the framework reuses the navigation half.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/router` — `defineRoutes(record)` returns a table whose one operation
  is `match(pathname)`; `<Router routes>` mounts it on the Navigation API and
  `<Outlet />` renders the rest of the matched stack; a branch's `error`
  component (`{ error, reset }` props, type `ErrorComponent`) renders in the
  layout's hole when what is below throws, keyed by `NavigationGeneration`
  so leaving the page clears it. `href(pattern, params?)`
  and `navigateTo(pattern, params?, options?)` build and perform navigations
  from the pattern **string** alone — no table import, so no cycle — with
  params inferred from the literal and the pattern itself checked once
  `interface Register { routes }` is augmented. `useParams(pattern)` returns
  typed params and throws if rendered under a different pattern; under the
  framework `Register` also carries `params` — the type each pattern's
  `paramsSchema` produces — so `href` takes a param as the page receives it
  (`ParsedParams` / `ParsedParamsMap` / `ParamsSchemaFor` are the types the
  generated code uses); `useRoute()`
  is the untyped form. `RouteOf<typeof routes>` is the pathname union to feed
  `@k8ordo/state`'s `Register`. `usePathname()` reads the platform's
  pathname — never the search — so it works with or without a table, which
  makes it the location hook that also works under the framework;
  `useMatch(pattern)` / `matchPath(pattern, pathname)` answer whether that
  pattern — or, with a trailing `/*`, anything strictly below it — is the pathname
  showing, with its params, table-free, so a sidebar can ask which section is
  open under the framework too; `normalizePathname(pathname)` is the router's
  own trailing-slash rule;
  `<PathnameProvider pathname>` seeds it for a server render and hydration,
  and is mounted by `<Router>` and by both mode runtimes, never by an
  application. `useInterceptedNavigation({claim, load, apply})` returns
  `{ generation }` and is the
  navigation primitive `<Router>` is built on, and the seam the framework
  uses to render server-produced trees instead.

---

# @k8ordo/static

> Builds a k8ordo application into files: every route rendered ahead of time,
> output a directory a static host can serve. The mode is the dependency —
> installing this package means Server Actions and request-time data do not
> exist as APIs. `src/routes/` is the pathname space (page/layout/not-found,
> `[param]`, `(group)`, `_private`), a page or layout may `export const paramsSchema` (any Standard Schema, synchronous)
> to type its parameters — a refused value makes the pattern not answer, so the
> walk goes on to `not-found.tsx` — an `error.tsx` shows in place of what
> throws below it (in the browser; at build time a page that throws stops the
> build), a `redirect.ts` is written as a page that sends the visitor on, a
> page renders its own `<title>` (React 19 hoists it), boundaries are React's
> own `'use client'`
> with `server-only` modules barred from the client bundle, and the route table
> and type wiring are generated rather than hand-written.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/static/docs/GUIDE.md): setup, the `routes/` grammar and what it refuses,
  execution boundaries, the build output, supplying pathnames for
  parameterised routes, and what static mode cannot do.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/static` — `framework(options?)` returns the Vite plugins for a
  static application (the same name `@k8ordo/server` exports, so the mode is
  the import and nothing else). `options.routesDir` moves the route directory (default
  `src/routes`); `options.paths` supplies concrete pathnames for routes with
  parameters, and a parameterised route left uncovered fails the build;
  `options.site` (the origin) makes the build also write `sitemap.xml`. A
  `'use server'` module fails it too — in `vite dev` as well as the build: a
  file cannot receive a Server Action, so the application wants
  `@k8ordo/server` instead.

---

# @k8ordo/server

> Runs a k8ordo application: every request answered by rendering, so route
> parameters need no list of values, an unknown URL is a real 404, and a form
> can post to a Server Action.
> The mode is the dependency — the alternative is `@k8ordo/static`, which
> renders every route at build time. `src/routes/` is the pathname space
> (page/layout/not-found, `[param]`, `(group)`, `_private`), a page or layout
> may `export const paramsSchema` (any Standard Schema, synchronous) to type its
> parameters — a refused value makes the pattern not answer, so the walk goes
> on to `not-found.tsx` under a real 404 — an `error.tsx` shows in place of
> what throws below it, a `redirect.ts` answers 307/308, a Server Action ends
> with `redirect()` (303 without JavaScript, a navigation with it), a page
> receives `request` (read-only headers and cookies) and renders its own
> `<title>` — boundaries are React's own `'use client'` with `server-only`
> modules barred from the client bundle, and the route table and type wiring are generated rather than
> hand-written.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/server/docs/GUIDE.md): setup, the `routes/` grammar and what it refuses,
  execution boundaries, building and running, and what running buys over
  static.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/server` — `framework(options?)` returns the Vite plugins for an
  application that runs (the same name `@k8ordo/static` exports, so the mode
  is the import and nothing else); `options.routesDir` moves the route directory
  (default `src/routes`). `serve({ dist?, port?, host? })` serves a build and returns
  `{ port, url, close }` (`port: 0` takes a free port):
  the client build's files as they are, everything else through the request
  handler. The built handler is a plain
  `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>` default-exported from
  `dist/rsc/index.js`, so another host can run it directly. `serve` only ever answers a
  request from a file inside the client build, whatever the pathname is
  spelled like. `redirect(to, { permanent? })` ends a Server Action by sending
  the visitor to `to`; `RouteRequest` is the type of the `request` prop.

---

# @k8ordo/i18n

> The locale axis of an application, owned. `defineLocales(['ja', 'en'])`
> declares the set once and derives membership, negotiation, the URL segment
> (`localize` / `delocalize`), and the `[locale]` params schema in the shape
> `@k8ordo/static` / `@k8ordo/server` run. `defineDictionary(locales, { ja,
> en })` holds the messages — strings, or functions of the values a message
> needs — typed by the default locale's shape (`Translations<typeof ja>`), so
> an untranslated key does not compile. `dictionary.translator(locale)` is
> `t` on the server; `<LocaleProvider locale>` (a string, renderable from a
> Server Component) and `useTranslation(dictionary)` are the client side.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/i18n/docs/GUIDE.md): what the package owns and does not (the locale
  segment, not the pathname; no message grammar; no lazy loading), the locale
  set and negotiation, the dictionary and `Translations`, the server
  translator, the client provider and hook, where the locale comes from (the
  URL; `/` redirects by `navigator.languages` or `Accept-Language`), `<html
  lang>`, static path expansion, and pairing with `@k8ordo/router` /
  `@k8ordo/ui` / `@k8ordo/form`.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/i18n` — `defineLocales(all, { default? })` returns `{ all,
  default, is, negotiate, localize, delocalize, paramsSchema }`; the first
  entry is the default unless told otherwise, every tag must be BCP 47, and
  `negotiate(list)` tries each requested tag in order (exact, then language)
  before falling back to the default. `parseAcceptLanguage(header)` turns an
  `Accept-Language` header into that list. `defineDictionary(locales, { …
  })` returns `{ locales, messages, translator(locale) }`; `translator` is
  `t(key, ...args)` for one locale and returns the same function for the
  same locale. `LocaleProvider` (client) carries a string locale;
  `useLocale()` reads it, `useLocale(locales)` reads it checked and typed;
  `useTranslation(dictionary)` returns `{ t, locale }`. Types:
  `Locales`, `LocaleOf`, `Dictionary`, `Translations`, `Translator`,
  `MessageKeyOf`, `Message`, `Messages`, `Translation`, `Delocalized`,
  `LocaleParamsSchema`.
